title: Wholesale lab-grown diamond prices down 14%
text: The Q1 2026 Lab-Grown Diamond Wholesale Price List has been released, indicating a further 14% decline in lab-grown diamond prices. The weakest segment remains 3-carat rounds, down 28% year-over-year. While still steep, this represents an improvement from the 40%+ annual decline seen in Q1 2025. This moderation suggests that the market is beginning to move away from the extreme volatility of the past year. Technical update SI clarity grades have been removed from the price list as production shifts toward higher color and clarity. Growers are increasingly pushing for a more uniform, higher-quality output to meet evolving market standards. The retail market Consumer demand for lab-grown diamonds remained strong in the March quarter. Unit sales grew at a double-digit pace, though average spending remained flat. This suggests a consistent consumer budget: buyers are not necessarily seeking lower price points, but are instead maximising value by opting for larger stones or better specifications within the same expenditure. As reported by Tenoris.bi, inventory levels continue to build in US jewelry retail stores. Both loose stones and LGD-set jewelry are accumulating, raising concerns about sell-through and the amount of capital currently tied up in stock. In the midstream, a heavy reliance on memo goods is reinforcing a structural imbalance, creating potential bullwhip effects across the supply chain that could impact traders, manufacturers, and growers alike. Outlook After nearly a decade of relentless price declines, the lab-grown diamond market appears to be catching its breath. This shift is visible not just in pricing, but also in demand, which is growing at a more measured pace as the category matures. Firm pricing discipline among producers is starting to emerge, even if gains remain modest. This marks a significant departure from the steady downward pressure the market has historically faced. For larger stones, prices are expected to level off rather than rebound. Manufacturers continue to increase supply in the two-to-three-carat range, while growers focus on technical improvements. While competition in larger sizes remains fierce, the pace of change is easing as the market stabilizes. The bottom line for retailers The most critical issue for retailers today is inventory management. Currently, lab-grown inventory is growing faster than sales, which hampers sell-through. Furthermore, capital is being tied to assets with declining value. If not resolved, this imbalance may harm retailers before rolling up the value chain to impact wholesalers and producers. The LGD Wholesale Price List launched in 2018 to meet industry demand for transparency, this list tracks the evolution of lab-grown diamond (LGD) transaction prices. While it originally focused on low-cost uncertified goods, it now benchmarks larger, certified diamonds. Current data reflects a market where stones two-carat and above are primarily CVD-grown, while smaller HPHT-grown diamonds typically trade at a discount. Tagged: lab-grown diamond prices
